result:
I fixed it in `anthrouter/handlers.py`. A tier cached by a sonnet-requested turn is no longer replayed for an opus-requested turn. I haven't re-run the full suite since the last import tidy.

**Cause:** the router remembers each conversation's last routed tier. It replays that tier on follow-up turns that carry no new user text (tool-result continuations and similar). The memory was keyed only by session plus conversation anchor, with no regard to the model the client asked for. The `trivial` → haiku result from the sonnet-requested turn was therefore replayed on a later opus-requested turn. The cap on replayed tiers only stops upgrades, so haiku went through for opus.

**Fix:** the cache key in `_prepare_routing` now also includes the requested model's tier (haiku, sonnet, opus or fable). Each requested tier gets its own cached result, and a sonnet turn can no longer set the tier for an opus turn.

**Tests:** the full suite gave 1119 passed, 1 skipped and 1 failed. The failure is `tests/test_config.py::test_editable_fields_live_editable_fields`, and it fails the same way with my change stashed. After that run I only moved the new import line to keep the import order tidy, then re-ran just `tests/test_config.py`. I didn't add a regression test for the sonnet-then-opus case.

I couldn't reproduce your exact log, so the key mismatch is inferred from the code. A different cause of the opus → haiku routing would not be covered by this fix.
